distance_note: Piers 38 and 40, at the foot of King St/Townsend St (89 King St), sit about 420-460m north of Mission Rock's own tracked boundary (Pier 48/50), just north of and adjacent to South Beach Harbor.
summary: A long-stalled Port of San Francisco redevelopment of Piers 38 and 40, led by San Francisco Waterfront Partners (an affiliate of Pacific Waterfront Partners). The original 2021 Exclusive Negotiating Agreement expired in 2023 after missed performance dates; in April 2026 the Port Commission settled a related back-rent dispute and adopted an Amended and Restated ENA giving the developer a 12-month "Evaluation Period" to rework the project's scope and financing. No lease, term sheet or CEQA review is in place as of this record's last_verified date.

milestones.text: Port Commission Resolution 21-10 authorizes an Exclusive Negotiating Agreement (dated 2021-03-12) with San Francisco Waterfront Partners III, LLC.

Port Commission Resolution 22-36 endorses a Term Sheet (never executed) describing the project's then-scope: visitor-serving restaurant/retail, maritime uses including South Beach Harbor expansion and youth sailing, retained Pier 40 marina tenants, public access/open space, and revenue-generating office space.
The original Exclusive Negotiating Agreement expires; the developer is out of compliance with its own performance dates.
Pacific Waterfront Partners (SFWP's affiliate) vacates three unrelated Port leases (Pier 28 and two Agriculture Building suites), leaving over $980,000 in back rent unpaid.

Port Commission adopts a Settlement Agreement (Resolution 26-21: Pacific Waterfront Partners to pay $720,000 over 3 years, with the remaining debt forgiven on compliance) and an Amended and Restated ENA (Resolution 26-22: a 12-month "Evaluation Period" for the developer to pursue value engineering, project phasing and a new financial partner, with a new Schedule of Performance due before the period ends around April 2027).

A marketing listing ("Pacific Cornerstone") offers up to approximately 279,876 sq ft of Piers 38 & 40 for long-term lease to credit tenants, positioning occupancy for late 2029 -- parallel tenant-marketing activity alongside the Port's own Evaluation Period, not a confirmed lease or Port-approved deal.

facts.value: San Francisco Waterfront Partners III, LLC (SFWP), an affiliate of Pacific Waterfront Partners (PWP)

As last formally endorsed (2022, never executed): approximately 215,000 sq ft office, up to 20,000 sq ft retail, approximately 130,000 sq ft public access/open space; cost estimate approximately $528-536 million, up from an original approximately $383 million 2020 proposal. Explicitly under review ("value engineering", "scope reduction") under the 2026 Amended ENA and not current.

open_questions: No Port Commission agenda item after 2026-04-28 was found; the 12-month Evaluation Period runs to approximately April 2027 with an interim Schedule of Performance due before then -- worth a periodic re-check rather than treating April 2026 as the final word.
No current, authoritative square footage or cost figure exists for the project as of this record's last_verified date: the 2022 estimates are explicitly being re-evaluated under the 2026 Amended ENA.

No public official's or community/maritime-advocacy group's position on the 2026 Amended ENA or settlement specifically has been found and sourced (all community-input coverage found dates to the 2020 RFP era).

Given the project's history of default and its ongoing, unresolved Evaluation Period, its ultimate outcome is genuinely uncertain -- this record treats it as an active but fragile project worth continued tracking, not a settled one.
